Middleware

Middleware runs before a request reaches your route handler, on every request that matches its matcher. It is the right place for redirects, rewrites, and header manipulation, and the wrong place for anything that needs a database — the middleware runtime has no filesystem and no persistent connections.

Defining middleware

Export a function named middleware from middleware.ts at the root of your project. The file is discovered by convention; there is no configuration entry that points at it, and a file in any other location is ignored silently.

export function middleware(request: Request) {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  if (url.pathname === "/old") {
    return Response.redirect(new URL("/new", url));
  }
}

Matchers

A matcher limits which paths the middleware runs on. Narrowing the matcher is the single most effective way to reduce middleware overhead, because a request that does not match never invokes the function at all.

  • /docs/:path* matches every path under /docs.
  • /((?!api|_next).*) matches everything except API routes and build assets.

Execution order

Middleware runs after redirects declared in configuration and before route handlers. When several matchers overlap, the middleware still runs exactly once per request; matchers select requests, they do not stack. See deployment for how middleware behaves on each supported runtime.
